Extract a complete character bible, location bible, and element bible from the script within the USER_SCRIPT tags. The script has a numbered line gutter ("N: ") — report lineNumbers from it, but never treat the gutter as script text.

<ELEMENTS>
The following user-uploaded elements are available. Produce an elementBible entry for each one used in the script:
- BROADCAST_MIC: A large-diaphragm condenser studio microphone with a champagne/silver metallic finish, cylindrical body topped by a domed fine wire-mesh grille. The body bears an arched logo emblem near the top, and below it the text "PHANTOM classic" in printed lettering, with a serial marking "Nr.1307" near the base. The mic sits cradled in a silver metal spider shock mount with curved wire arms and rubber bands holding it, mounted on a black stand with an adjustable lever clamp. Behind it, a round black mesh pop filter on a curved black gooseneck arm is positioned in front of the mic's grille.
</ELEMENTS>

<USER_SCRIPT>
1: CORAL — A SUMMER LAUNCH
2: 
3: A launch film shot between shifts. Scarlett Doyle, 19, sells frozen pineapple at the Bondi kiosk and has 40 minutes before her break ends. She has one take, one shade, and a wave with bad timing. Voice: bright, wry, unbothered.
4: 
5: Scene 1 — 6s
6: INT. BONDI SHARE-HOUSE LAUNDRY — MORNING. A folding table jammed against a white tiled wall, ring light clipped to the dryer, a phone on a tripod. Scarlett — blonde, sun-freckled, kiosk polo half-tucked — drops into frame, slaps a cardboard mailer onto the table and rips the tape in one motion. Sunlight through the louvre window throws hard clean stripes across white cardboard and tissue paper. Handheld, slight micro-shake, eye-level. She looks up at the phone and says, "Okay — forty minutes. Go."
7: 
8: Scene 2 — 5s
9: MACRO, LOCKED. Fingers peel back cream tissue and lift a coral lipstick free of its bed — matte white tube, brushed gold band, condensation of morning light along the edge. Her thumb clicks the cap off and the coral bullet twists up, catching a bright specular flare. Shallow depth, warm highlights, crisp white ground.
10: 
11: Scene 3 — 5s
12: CLOSE, off-mirror angle over her shoulder. She swipes the coral once across her lower lip, presses her lips together, and immediately grins at her own reflection — no ceremony, cap already back on with a click. The tiled wall behind her glows white. Handheld drift in.
13: 
14: Scene 4 — 5s
15: OVERHEAD FLAT-LAY, locked, directly above. On a folded white towel: the coral tube, a set of kiosk keys, zinc-white sunscreen, a half-eaten frozen pineapple stick beading water, an elastic hair tie. Her hand enters, plucks the keys, and the towel shifts — the lipstick rolls a slow half-turn into the light and stops dead center.
16: 
17: Scene 5 — 6s
18: EXT. BONDI PROMENADE — LATE MORNING. Scarlett strides fast along the sea wall, phone held out at arm's length, hair lifting sideways in the wind, surfers cresting behind her in the mid-ground. She glances into the lens mid-stride and says, "Made for the water. Watch."
19: 
20: Scene 6 — 5s
21: EXT. KIOSK WINDOW. Direct on-camera flash, punchy editorial. Scarlett leans through the service hatch, coral mouth, hands sliding a paper cup of pineapple across the counter to a stranger's waiting fingers. Steam of cold — the cup sweats. She flicks her eyebrows at the lens. Locked frame, hard flash shadow on white paint.
22: 
23: Scene 7 — 5s
24: MACRO ON HER MOUTH AND JAW, three-quarter profile, sunlight raking. She drinks straight from a metal water bottle, a bead of water tracking down her chin; she wipes it away with the back of her wrist. The coral stays. Handheld, shallow focus.
25: 
26: Scene 8 — 6s
27: EXT. SHORELINE — AFTERNOON. She sets the phone-tripod in wet sand, backs up two steps into the frame, and starts her polished line — and a shorebreak wave surges in over her ankles, knocking the tripod sideways. The horizon tilts hard as the camera falls. Water rushes the lens. Handheld chaos, real light.
28: 
29: Scene 9 — 5s
30: LOW ANGLE, camera half-buried in wet sand at the waterline. The coral tube lies in the foam, gold band winking, as retreating water sluices around it and carves a bright channel in the sand. A tanned hand plunges in and snatches it up, dripping.
31: 
32: Scene 10 — 6s
33: EXT. SHORELINE, WIDER. Scarlett, soaked to the thigh, laughing so hard she doubles over, wet hair stuck to one cheek, tube held up in triumph. She straightens, pushes the hair back, and says to the lens, "Still on."
34: 
35: Scene 11 — 6s
36: FINAL FRAME. Late-afternoon glow, waist-up, salt drying white on her forearm. She rolls the coral bullet up, presses it once to her lips, clicks the cap shut and tosses the tube up — it flips once in the golden air and lands back in her palm as she turns toward the surf and walks in, ankle-deep, water flashing around her.
</USER_SCRIPT>
